source.title: No More Adam: Learning Rate Scaling at Initialization is All You Need
source.authors: Minghao Xu; Li-Chuan Xiang; Xu Cai; Hong-Kai Wen

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices; no garbling or cutoff apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests optimizer performance and hyperparameter robustness, but does not test whether networks that fit random labels generalize, nor the listed claim versions on training-to-test gaps or their predictors.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results comparing optimizers on classification and language tasks, plus profiling, but none directly measure fitting random labels, test gaps as a function of width, convolutional versus fully connected generalization, dropout effects, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. G-SNR values are used to set the proposed optimizer; they are not reported as a measure tracking training-to-test gap.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out performance of standard SGD/momentum SGD and adaptive optimizers on image classification and language generation. These results bear on V4; measuring a training-to-test gap is not required. The reader incorrectly excluded these comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that initialization-based parameter-group scaling lets SGD-SaI achieve performance comparable to or better than adaptive optimizers while reducing optimizer-state memory and update costs. They report hyperparameter robustness, acknowledge slower early convergence, and leave full training evaluation of larger language models unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces and evaluates an initialization-scaled SGD optimizer; its experiments compare task performance across optimizers rather than test the claim versions' generalization mechanisms.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported optimizer performance varies across hyperparameter search settings; the paper reports peak and average accuracy across a search for ViT-S/16 and CNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD-SaI nearly matches AdamW's peak ViT accuracy and has higher average accuracy across the tested hyperparameter grid.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization-based parameter-block learning-rate scaling can improve momentum SGD's performance and hyperparameter robustness relative to adaptive optimizers.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-2-small pretraining compares SGD-SaI with AdamW and Adam-mini, without a standard SGD baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD-SaI can achieve competitive language-model training and validation loss relative to adaptive optimizers.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimizer-state memory and optimizer-step runtime improve with SGD-SaI; larger language models receive profiling rather than full training evaluation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing adaptive second-moment updates can reduce optimizer memory and update costs.

record.problems: Several reported comparisons concern validation or evaluation performance across optimizer hyperparameter grids rather than a direct measurement of the claim's train-to-test gap. For larger language models, the authors report optimizer-step profiling only, not full training results; diffusion fine-tuning is assessed qualitatively.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the reported outcomes concern optimizer performance, memory, and runtime and do not measure an object named in the claim versions.

untested.parts: Widening beyond the width required for interpolation.

The exact learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning regime; matched training performance across optimizers; switching optimizers; word-level language-model comparisons against standard SGD. The image experiments also tune weight decay.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Extract Table 2's standard optimizer comparisons, including peak accuracies and uncertainty. Also record grid-average accuracies separately: SGDM 14.33%, Adam 20.93%, Adam-mini 36.65%, AdamW 37.21%. Grid averages measure performance across sampled configurations and must not be substituted for best-tuned performance.

Extract Table 4's standard SGD versus AdamW and Adam-mini evaluation metrics. SGD versus AdamW: BLEU 66.6 versus 68.9; NIST 8.54 versus 8.69; MET 44.2 versus 46.5; ROUGE-L 68.2 versus 71.3; CIDEr 2.32 versus 2.51. Distinguish standard, scaled and proposed optimizers.

Recover standard SGD/SGDM versus Adam and AdamW test-accuracy comparisons from the CNN figures. The supplied text gives SGDM's ResNet-18 peak as 95.26%, but does not preserve the adaptive baselines' numerical peaks or sufficient histogram detail for directional verdicts.

record.verdict_notes: No existing rows require correction because the record contains none. Its blanket rows_left_out rationale is incorrect: baseline optimizer comparisons directly test V4 and need extraction. SGD-SaI's own performance alone does not establish the standard SGD comparison named in V4. The study is not an original source for V4.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error after widening beyond interpolation.
Whether adaptive optimizers generalize worse than SGD under limited tuning, including stated tuning and task qualifications.
Large-batch generalization gaps under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a correlate of the training-to-test gap.
Effect of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: ViT-S/16 trained from scratch on ImageNet-1k: peak Adam versus SGDM validation accuracy after learning-rate and weight-decay search.
relationships.reason: Table 2 reports Adam at 61.56 ± 0.93% versus SGDM at 63.80 ± 0.35%, consistent with an adaptive optimizer performing worse in this setting; based on text because rows are missing.
relationships.display_finding: Reported peak validation accuracy is 61.56±0.93% for Adam versus 63.80±0.35% for momentum SGD, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: ViT-S/16 on ImageNet-1k: peak performance of AdamW, Adam-mini and Prodigy versus SGDM.
relationships.reason: Table 2 reports 73.04%, 72.29% and 73.24%, respectively, versus SGDM's 63.80%; the adaptive disadvantage does not extend to these optimizers under this recipe, which includes weight-decay tuning; based on text.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW, Adam-mini and Prodigy reportedly exceeded momentum SGD accuracy with weight-decay tuning, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: GPT-2-medium LoRA fine-tuning on E2E with the reported default hyperparameters.
relationships.reason: Table 4 reports AdamW outperforming standard SGD on all five evaluation metrics, including BLEU 68.9 versus 66.6; this extends the language-task qualifications beyond word-level modeling; based on text because rows are missing.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW reportedly exceeded SGD on all five evaluation metrics, but this comparison remains unverified.
